This is the highest level for this average since November 20, 2021 when it was 2,004,250.

There were 239,379 initial claims in the comparable week in 2024.

notes: DOL weekly claims news release exactly as served (9 pages, US Letter, made with Microsoft Word, tagged). Page 1: 'News Release' masthead with the DOL seal and social icons (not checked: may be images), the embargo line, the release title, 'SEASONALLY ADJUSTED DATA' and two paragraphs, two line charts. Page 2: 'UNADJUSTED DATA', two paragraphs, two charts, four short paragraphs. Page 3: two paragraphs. Page 4: three tables with footnotes. Page 5: advance state claims. Page 6: weekly seasonally adjusted series. Page 7: state table for the prior week. Page 8: states with changes over 1,000. Page 9: technical notes, contacts. Headings: the release has no bold or large headings; its section titles are body-size lines in capitals ('UNEMPLOYMENT INSURANCE WEEKLY CLAIMS', 'TECHNICAL NOTES'), underlined capitals ('SEASONALLY ADJUSTED DATA', 'UNADJUSTED DATA') and the lettered technical-note titles; these seven are listed. Table titles in capitals (pages 4 and 8) and above the tables of pages 5-6 are captions, not headings; the underlined 'FOOTNOTES' label under the page-4 tables is a notes label and is not listed. Tables: the two page-4 blocks under one title are listed as two tables because a blank line and a repeated 'WEEK ENDING' row separate them. Superscript footnote digits are written attached to the word ('Prior Year¹', 'Benefits³'; NFKC makes them '1', '3'); 'STC / Workshare ⁵' keeps the visible space before its marker; whether the text layer has a space before a marker could not be seen. 'Nevada *' keeps its estimate mark (normalization deletes '*'). In the page-5 table the two group headers span three columns each and are written in the first column they cover; covered and empty cells are empty strings (not scored). The page-6 table is PARTIAL (header row plus 12 of 54 week rows; the last week has no insured-unemployment values, so those cells are empty); its stacked header lines are joined with spaces ('Change from Prior Week'). The page-7 table (13 columns, stacked three-line headers over two groups) is not checked: its header grouping cannot be written as one grid without guessing. Comment cells that wrap to a second line (page 8) are joined with a space. Signs: negative values and the spaced dash in 'Advance State Claims - Not Seasonally Adjusted' are written with ASCII hyphen-minus (printed hyphen-width; the code point could not be seen), so phrases and anchors avoid them, but table cells with negative values assume hyphen-minus. Arithmetic checked while typing: every Change cell equals the difference of its two columns, the page-5 state columns sum to the US Total row, the continued-weeks rows sum to TOTAL, and the page-6 4-week averages equal the mean of the last four weeks. must_contain: 25 phrases, each printed once, none containing an apostrophe or quotation mark ('previous week's', '"on"' are cut out). ordered: 7 body-text anchors on pages 1, 2, 2, 3, 5 (the note under the state table), 9, 9. Noise: only page numbers repeat, so noise is empty; the text is ragged-right with no line-end hyphenation, so absent is empty. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 90-230 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, mastheads, cover art, chart labels) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
